newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: ZCCM importing coal to fuel Nkana smelter.
newsitem.headline: ZCCM importing coal to fuel Nkana smelter.

text.p: Zambia Consoldiated Coppers Mines (ZCCM) said on Friday it had started importing coal from Zimbabwe following the closure of Zambia's largest coal mine to ensure uninterrupted operations at its Nkana smelter.

A ZCCM spokesman said that the company, which uses an average 250 tonnes of coal per day, was importing coal from from Zimbabwe's Wankie mine as a result of the closure of Zambia's Maamba mine due to flooding.

"Nkana Division of ZCCM has taken measures to try and ensure that smelter operations at the division, which uses the bulk of Maamba coal, are not disrupted following closure of Maamba mine due to floods which have devastated the small mining town in the Southern Province," the spokesman said.
"Since it is not known when operations at Maamba coal mine will return to normal, Nkana Division has started importing coal from Wankie in Zimbabwe."
Nkana was also using its strategic stockpile of coal to ensure smelter operations continued uninterrupted.
"The measures put in place should be adequate to sustain smelter operations at the division," the spokesman said.
The government said on Thursday it was battling to restore water and power supplies to the mining town of Maamba after heavy flooding in the area over the past few days.

Southern Province permanent secretary Sylvester Mpishi said residents had been living without clean water, electricity and medical supplies for days after heavy rain washed away key installations in the town.
The rain disrupted production at Zambia's largest coal mine, Maamba Collieries Ltd, after its open pit was flooded and equipment at its central works was damaged.
Mpishi said there was no indication when the mine would resume normal operations.
The Zambian Privatisation Agency put the mine up for sale in October last year. It has the capacity to produce 600,000 to 800,000 metric tonnes per year.
